params.body:
Tests and documentation only. No behaviour is changed, nothing is refactored. These are characterization tests: they pin what the publishing path does **today**, warts included, so that the clean-up after the cutover has something to fail against.

Before this, nothing in the suite touched `send_to_modix`, `WebhookHelper`, the publishing branches of `VehicleObserver` or Nederland Mobiel.

## What the path does

The vehicle flag `send_to_modix` (labelled "Portalen" on screen) decides whether a vehicle goes out. Despite the name, Modix is not the receiver any more.

`VehicleObserver` turns a change into a type: the flag going to 1 sends `create`, going to 0 sends `delete`, and a sale sends `sold` and then clears the flag. A vehicle that is *created* complete and with the flag already on sends `create` straight away, from `created`: the flag never has to go dirty. `triggerWebhook` only dispatches when the vehicle is complete and (the flag is on, or the type is `delete` or `sold`), so a removal leaves even with the flag off and a half-finished vehicle never leaves at all.

**The message is a doorbell, not a parcel.** No vehicle data goes out. Every receiver gets the same four fields: the method plus the three identifiers configured in `webhook_fields` (vehicle, dealer, user). The receiver then comes and fetches the full record through the Passport partner API (`VehicleApiController::detail`). A lost message is therefore a missed cue, not lost data.

Which receivers a vehicle reaches: the rows of its own dealer plus the rows with no dealer. The four per-receiver flags do not choose **who** is rung, only **what** they are told: every receiver of the dealer is rung for every type, and a switched-off type is translated (`sold` becomes `delete`, `create` becomes `update`). `update` and `delete` have no translation and are sent even when switched off.

Everything outbound sits behind `Outbound::impact('webhooks')` / `('nederlandmobiel')`, so nothing leaves a non-production environment.

## What is now pinned

`tests/Feature/VehiclePublishingTest.php`, 21 tests, tagged `@rule S2-10.*`:

- ticking the flag dispatches one `create` per applicable receiver; creating with the flag on does the same immediately
- unticking dispatches `delete`; selling dispatches `sold` and clears the flag
- `delete` and `sold` leave without the flag, `create` and `update` do not
- an incomplete vehicle dispatches nothing at all, while the rest of the sold path still runs
- `resolveWebhookType` in all its cases, including the two types with no translation
- receiver selection (own dealer plus the global rows) and what `$force` does to the dealer lookup
- the payload: exactly the mapped fields, the identifiers put through `ApiHelper::encrypt`, and no price, chassis number or mileage anywhere in the body
- the seal closed: no job queued and no request sent, for webhooks and for Nederland Mobiel; and the same with the seal open, so the test measures the seal and not a dead path
- a failing receiver is written to `webhook_logs` and does not break the save

## What surprised us

Three findings, recorded as X rows rather than fixed here:

- **X-97** The sold branch is not guarded by `isDirty`. It tests `filled($vehicle->sold_at) || filled($vehicle->sold_price) || $vehicle->sold == 1`, and those stay true forever, so **every later save of a sold vehicle rings `sold` again** at every receiver, plus a second quiet save to clear the flag.
- **X-98** "Encrypted" in `webhook_fields` is `ApiHelper::encrypt`, which is `(value * 3) + 5`, reversed by `(value - 5) / 3`. That is obfuscation, not encryption. The damage is limited because an identifier on its own opens nothing (the partner API still wants a dealer token), but the column name promises something the code does not do.
- **X-99** Only a connection error counts as a failure. A receiver answering 4xx or 5xx throws nothing (there is no `throw()` on the call), is written to `webhook_logs` exactly like a success, and is never retried. A partner returning 500 for a week looks, from here, like a partner that processes everything.

Two smaller ones, pinned in the tests: without a session and without an API token the custom field falls through to the literal string `"not found "` (every doorbell rung by a queue worker, a console command or an import looks like this, R S2-10.9); and the `$type` argument of `getWebhooksForDealerForType` is never passed by any caller, so the filter it would apply has never run.

## Verdict on the three suspicions

**The two helper paths.** `dispatchVehicleWebhookJobs` (queued) is used only by `VehicleObserver::triggerWebhook`; `triggerVehicleWebhook` (inline) is used only by the console command `stocklist:forceUpdateWebhooks`. **Neither bypasses the seal.** The queued path is checked twice (in the observer before queueing, and again in the job), the inline path once, later, after the payload is built, but before anything is sent. Both are pinned with a closed-seal and an open-seal test. The problem is not a hole but three question points for one boundary. Open point O-23.

**The `modix_ftp_username` rule in `Vehicle::booted` (line 489).** Not dead, and **both can fire**: it only needs a logged-in user whose dealer has a Modix FTP username. It runs on `updating`, so it clears the flag in the same UPDATE statement, where the observer needs a second quiet save. They agree on the outcome, so the effect is invisible, and it is pinned in `test_the_modix_rule_and_the_observer_agree_on_clearing_the_flag`.

**The `deleted_at` column.** `webhooks` and `webhook_fields` both carry `deleted_at datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp()`, so every row is stamped as deleted the moment it is written. **Neither model uses SoftDeletes** (`BaseModel` extends `\Eloquent` plain), so nothing looks at the column and everything works today. It is a trap, not a defect: adding the trait would make every receiver disappear at once, silently. There is now a test that fails the moment the trait appears. Open point O-24.

## Proposal for after the cutover

Recorded as open points (O-22 to O-25), not as findings, because none of them is a defect today:

- a `VehiclePublisher` seam the observer talks to (`published()`, `unpublished()`, `sold()`, `removed()`), with the two helper paths folded into one and **the seal asked in exactly one place**
- rename `send_to_modix` to match its receivers
- make `deleted_at` nullable on both webhook tables, or drop it
- pull `removeFromNederlandMobiel` out of `OwnStockController`: an observer calling a controller with a base64-encoded id (and `Vehicle::booted` doing the same) belongs in the same clean-up

## Documentation

New chapter **S2-10 Het bericht aan de partner** in `docs/bedrijfsregels/12-s2-eigen-wagenpark-publiceren.md`: the doorbell plus the pull, the global receivers and the per-dealer ones, the per-type translation, and what happens when the message never arrives (three attempts, then silence, with `webhook_logs` kept five days by `stocklist:daily`). Eleven rules, all eleven with a test. `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated.
params.title: Publishing to the portals: tests for what it already does
